title: Reading and analysing PIONIRS data with mnirs
text: PIONIRS .ftn(2) files recognised automatically. channels specified, read_mnirs() returns "Time" time_channel, "TagLabel" event_channel, “StO2” channels nirs_channels. automatically detecting known NIRS device file format, columns returned allow exploration file. filter_mnirs() applies digital filter nirs_channels automatically retrieved metadata data frame class “mnirs” read . , Butterworth low-pass 2nd-order filter cutoff frequency 0.05 Hz seems smooth data sufficiently.

text: Channels can also specified renamed explicitly. Since already read file, can instead modify channels using create_mnirs_data(). specify raw haemoglobin concentration signals, event column containing manually entered labels.  correct_blood_volume() normalises oxy-, deoxy-, total[haem] changes blood volume occlusion. title: Reading and analysing PIONIRS data with mnirs
text: analyse_kinetics(method = "peak_slope") fits rolling linear regression algorithm across full interval, returns greatest (positive negative, depending direction) slope centred within specified time span. can specify different span parameter interval named list().
code: result_deoxy <- analyse_kinetics(     df_list,     method = "peak_slope",     span   = list(interval_1 = 120, interval_2 = 10) ) |>     print() #>  #> Peak Linear Response Rate #>     Model Coefficients: #>     interval nirs_channels start_time  slope intercept peak_slope_time #> 1 interval_1           hhb       91.0 0.1987    -2.174              82 #> 2 interval_2           hhb        391 -5.988     93.59              14  plot(result_deoxy)

title: Reading and analysing PIONIRS data with mnirs
text: Now let’s look advanced kinetics analysis methods can fit reoxygenation hyperaemia window. method = "monoexponential" fits exponential curve data. end_window = 30 dynamically ends fitting window first peak trough (depending direction) extreme values within 30 sec, avoiding post-hyperaemic decay toward baseline non-asymptotic bias monoexponential time constant coefficient.  experimental kinetics analysis methods (still development yet validated), can avoid potential coefficient bias modelling hyperaemic drift secondary linear slope component two-phase “exponential-linear” kinetics response. method = "exponential_drift" ("exponential_linear") fits linear slope term primary monoexponential response, separate fast reoxygenation phase slow hyperaemic drift.  method = "biexponential" another experimental method fits two-phase response overlapping fast slow monoexponential curves.  Fit diagnostics stored results$diagnostics can used statistically qualitatively compare models. Information criteria (aic, aicc, bic) can used compare models different numbers parameters (n_params). Lower values represent statistically “better” fitting models, penalising extra parameters (criterion uses slightly different weights may disagree marginal differences). However, case, model fit different number samples (n_obs) addition parameters, information criteria used statistically conclude better fit. model diagnostics can used qualitative comparators, “best” model can chosen based physiological expectations, experimental design, established validity. Caution Two-phase Exponential-drift Biexponential kinetics currently experimental methods yet validated. example, r2, rmse, snr (signal--noise ratio) suggest biexponential model capturing shape full hyperaemic decay return baseline, well exponential-linear drift model hyperaemic component alone.
code: result_monoexp <- analyse_kinetics(     df_list[2],     method     = "monoexponential",     end_window = 30  ## includes 30-sec after the first local extrema ) |>     print() #>  #> Monoexponential One-Phase Kinetics #>     Model Coefficients: #>     interval nirs_channels start_time     A      B    TD   tau      k   MRT #> 1 interval_2           hhb        391 48.98 -39.70 9.421 6.563 0.1524 15.98  plot(result_monoexp, time_labels = TRUE) result_drift <- analyse_kinetics(     df_list[2],     method     = "exponential_drift",     end_window = 180  ## includes more of the hyperaemic response ) |>     print() #>  #> Exponential-Linear Drift Two-Phase Kinetics #>     Model Coefficients: #>     interval nirs_channels start_time             model     A      B    TD #> 1 interval_2           hhb        391 exponential_drift 49.00 -42.91 9.258 #>     tau      k   MRT  texc slope_B #> 1 7.343 0.1362 16.60 42.21  0.1409  plot(result_drift, time_labels = TRUE) result_biexp <- analyse_kinetics(     df_list[2],     method = "biexponential"     ## `end_window = Inf` by default; fitting to the full data available ) |>     print() #>  #> Biexponential Two-Phase Kinetics #>     Model Coefficients: #>     interval nirs_channels start_time         model     A      B    TD   tau #> 1 interval_2           hhb        391 biexponential 48.98 -50.77 9.112 8.287 #>     MRT  texc     B2  tau2 #> 1 17.40 42.49 -5.639 173.7  plot(result_biexp, time_labels = TRUE) rbind(     monoexponential   = result_monoexp$diagnostics,     exponential_drift = result_drift$diagnostics,     biexponential     = result_biexp$diagnostics ) #>                     interval nirs_channels n_obs n_params        r2    adj_r2 #> monoexponential   interval_2           hhb    66        4 0.9931830 0.9928532 #> exponential_drift interval_2           hhb   216        5 0.9947398 0.9946401 #> biexponential     interval_2           hhb   301        6 0.9908865 0.9907320 #>                       rmse    cv_rmse      snr       aic      aicc       bic #> monoexponential   2.724835 0.15514626 21.66407  329.6177  330.6177  340.5660 #> exponential_drift 1.418235 0.05774017 22.78996  775.9280  776.3299  796.1796 #> biexponential     1.617703 0.07245608 20.40315 1157.7672 1158.1495 1183.7170

text: data function takes data frame list data frames, analyses channels separately, returns single formatted table results. Model components coefficients, fitted data frames, intake metadata, diagnostics can retrieved results metadata results$.... nirs_channels & time_channel data contain “mnirs” metadata, detected automatically; otherwise can specified explicitly. start_time, direction, & end_window arguments apply every method. start_time marks response onset. intervals come extract_intervals(), retrieved automatically “mnirs” metadata. Otherwise defaults first non-negative time value (.e. 0).direction detects whether response rises (“positive”) falls (“negative”), defaults “auto”. parametric fits also constrains expected response direction, case ambiguous kinetics. deoxy[haem], specify direction = "positive", since deoxygenation increases occlusions.end_window defines end fitting window looking forward reasonable end time, taking first peak trough (rising falling response, respectively) extreme value within span. default end_window = Inf uses global extreme across whole interval, appropriate short occlusion windows. method Multiple analysis methods currently available. OxCap analysis uses “peak_slope” “monoexponential”, “exponential_drift” exploratory extension . method = "peak_slope" peak slope method semi-parametric approach: fits linear regression model across rolling local window, returning single steepest slope along time occurs. OxCap analysis, steepest local rate deoxygenation interpreted point greatest mismatch O2 delivery extraction — proxy mV̇O2 occlusion. width, span local window specified either width (number samples) span (range time units time_channel). want peak slope 3-sec span within occlusion interval. align window can “centre”-aligned around target sample (idx), “left”-aligned idx start (forward-looking), “right”-aligned idx end (backward-looking). keep default align = "centre". partial default, local window returns linear regression model samples within valid. partial = TRUE, windows return slope model long two samples available. Windows fewer samples tend return steeper slopes, may relevant interpretation — e.g. edges noisy dataset, two samples alone can produce extreme local slope usually want ignore.  Tip Individual kinetics results can quickly visualised built-plot() function coefficient labels (see ?plot.mnirs_kinetics). Next, can recursively analyse resulting slope coefficients another analyse_kinetics() call using “monoexponential” model estimate mV̇O2 recovery.

code: ## use 3-param monoexponential model without TD ## fit samples in sequence grouped by trial ## channels must be specified explicitly monoexp_results <- analyse_kinetics(     slope_results,     nirs_channels   = slope,  ## supply predictor & response channels     time_channel    = peak_slope_time,     method          = "monoexponential",     use_TD          = FALSE,     group_intervals = list(trial1 = 1:16, trial2 = 17:32),     zero_time       = TRUE    ## rebase each trial start_time to zero )  ## view the formatted results monoexp_results #> #> Monoexponential One-Phase Kinetics #>     Model Coefficients: #>   interval nirs_channels     A      B TD   tau       k   MRT #> 1   trial1     hhb_slope 1.051 0.2104 NA 19.33 0.05174 19.33 #> 2   trial2     hhb_slope 1.034 0.1666 NA 15.39 0.06496 15.39 ## extract tau and k coef labels per trial, for plotting coef_labels <- monoexp_results$coefficients |>     summarise(         .by = interval,         label = sprintf(             "Trial %s\ntau = %s sec\nk = %s min⁻¹",             gsub("trial", "", interval),             round(tau, 1),             round(k * 60, 1) ## convert to min^-1         )     ) ## add custom info to the plot plot(monoexp_results, time_labels = TRUE, points = TRUE, labels = FALSE) +     labs(         x = "Occlusion Times (mm:ss)",         y = expression(bold(HHb ~ Slope ~ '(' * μM %.% sec^'-1' * ')')),     ) +      theme(legend.position = "none") +      geom_text(         data = coef_labels, aes(label = label),         x = Inf, y = Inf, size = 5, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3     )

code: library(ggplot2) ## for plotting library(mnirs) #>  #> Attaching package: 'mnirs' #> The following object is masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     SSgompertz  ## {mnirs} includes sample files from a few mNIRS devices example_mnirs() #> [1] "artinis_intervals.xlsx"  "moxy_intervals.csv"      #> [3] "moxy_ramp.xlsx"          "pionirs_occlusion.ftn"   #> [5] "portamon_oxcap.xlsx"     "train.red_intervals.csv"  ## rename channels in the format `renamed = "original_name"` ## where "original_name1" should match the file column name exactly data_raw <- read_mnirs(     file_path = example_mnirs("moxy_ramp"), ## call an example data file     nirs_channels = c(         smo2_left = "SmO2 Live",    ## identify and rename channels         smo2_right = "SmO2 Live(2)"     ),     time_channel = c(time = "hh:mm:ss"), ## date-time format will be converted to numeric     event_channel = NULL,           ## leave blank if unused     sample_rate = NULL,             ## if blank, will be estimated from time_channel     add_timestamp = FALSE,          ## omit a date-time timestamp column     zero_time = TRUE,               ## recalculate time values from zero     keep_all = FALSE,               ## return only the specified data channels     verbose = TRUE                  ## show warnings & messages ) #> ! Estimated `sample_rate` = 2 Hz. #> ℹ Define `sample_rate` explicitly to override. #> Warning in read_mnirs(): ! Duplicate or irregular `time_channel` samples detected. #> ℹ time = 211.59 and 1183.6. #> ℹ Re-sample with `mnirs::resample_mnirs()`.  ## Note the above info message that sample_rate was estimated correctly at 2 Hz 👆 ## ignore the warnings about irregular sampling for now, we will resample later  data_raw #> # A tibble: 2,202 × 3 #>     time smo2_left smo2_right #>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> #>  1 0            54         68 #>  2 0.560        54         68 #>  3 1.11         54         66 #>  4 1.66         54         66 #>  5 2.21         54         66 #>  6 2.76         54         66 #>  7 3.31         57         67 #>  8 3.86         57         67 #>  9 4.41         57         67 #> 10 4.96         57         67 #> # ℹ 2,192 more rows  ## note the `time_labels` plot argument to display time values as `h:mm:ss` plot(     data_raw,     time_labels = TRUE,     na.omit = FALSE )

what: replace_mnirs(): Replace local outliers, invalid values, and missing values
title: Muscle Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Processing and Analysis
code: data_cleaned <- replace_mnirs(     data_resampled,     ## blank channels will be retrieved from metadata     invalid_values = 0, ## known invalid values in the data     invalid_above = 90, ## remove data spikes above 90     outlier_cutoff = 3, ## recommended default value     width = 7,          ## window to detect and replace outliers/missing values     method = "linear"   ## linear interpolation over `NA`s )  plot(data_cleaned, time_labels = TRUE)

title: Muscle Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Processing and Analysis
code: data_filtered <- filter_mnirs(     data_cleaned,           ## blank channels will be retrieved from metadata     method = "butterworth", ## Butterworth digital filter is a common choice     order = 2,              ## filter order number     W = 0.02,               ## filter fractional critical frequency `[0, 1]`     type = "low",           ## specify a "low-pass" filter     na.rm = TRUE            ## explicitly ignore NAs )  ## we will add the non-filtered data back to the plot to compare plot(data_filtered, time_labels = TRUE) +     geom_line(         data = data_cleaned,          aes(y = smo2_left, colour = "smo2_left"), alpha = 0.4     ) +     geom_line(         data = data_cleaned,          aes(y = smo2_right, colour = "smo2_right"), alpha = 0.4     )

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
text: Creates initial coefficient estimates selfStart wrapper around biexponential(), use stats::nls(). Supports 5-parameter (, B, tau, B2, tau2) 6-parameter forms adding time delay TD; arity inferred formula passed stats::nls().

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
code: SSbiexponential(t, A, B, tau, B2, tau2, TD)

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
text: t numeric vector predictor variable (time). numeric parameter starting value response variable (t = 0 intercept). B numeric parameter asymptote fast component; value fast response alone approach. tau numeric parameter fast time constant (\(\tau_1\)), units predictor variable t. Dominates initial steep response. B2 numeric parameter asymptote slow component; stable plateau response recovers toward t approaches infinity. tau2 numeric parameter slow time constant (\(\tau_2\)), units predictor variable t. Typically tau2 >> tau. TD numeric parameter time delay onset response, units predictor variable t. NULL (default), 5-parameter model without time delay used.

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
text: numeric vector predicted values length predictor variable t.

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
text: 5-parameter: x ~ SSbiexponential(t, , B, tau, B2, tau2) 6-parameter: x ~ SSbiexponential(t, , B, tau, B2, tau2, TD) two phases weakly identified tau tau2 close, algorithm = "port" time constants bounded non-negative control = nls.control(warnOnly = TRUE) recommended. analyse_kinetics() instead fits phases sequentially, holding fast phase near monoexponential estimate. 5-parameter form recommended small samples obvious time delay expected, converges reliably. stats::nls() reads free parameters formula right-hand side, omitting TD incurs degrees--freedom penalty. Starting estimates profiled coarse grid tau, tau2 (TD) amplitudes solved least squares grid point, keeping residual-minimising start. Grid pairs tau / tau2 > 0.98 dropped near-collinear. model function returns analytic gradient free parameters "gradient" attribute, stats::nls() resort stats::numericDeriv(). stats::predict() fitted model carries attribute; drop .vector().

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
text: parameter may held constant writing value place name formula, e.g. x ~ SSbiexponential(t, , B, tau = 5, B2, tau2) holds fast time constant 5. Fixed parameters excluded estimation returned stats::coef().

title: Self-starting biexponential model — SSbiexponential
code: ## create a biexponential excursion-recovery curve with random noise set.seed(13) t <- 0:120 x <- biexponential(t, A = 70, B = 40, tau = 5, B2 = 60, tau2 = 40) +     rnorm(length(t), 0, 0.8) data <- data.frame(t, x)  ## 5-parameter fit model <- nls(     x ~ SSbiexponential(t, A, B, tau, B2, tau2),     data = data,     algorithm = "port",     lower = c(-Inf, -Inf, 0, -Inf, 0),     control = nls.control(warnOnly = TRUE) ) summary(model) #>  #> Formula: x ~ SSbiexponential(t, A, B, tau, B2, tau2) #>  #> Parameters: #>      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> A     70.4808     0.5841  120.66   <2e-16 *** #> B     39.6287     1.0816   36.64   <2e-16 *** #> tau    5.1728     0.3067   16.86   <2e-16 *** #> B2    60.0822     0.3795  158.34   <2e-16 *** #> tau2  40.2967     3.4506   11.68   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.7524 on 116 degrees of freedom #>  #> Algorithm "port", convergence message: relative convergence (4) #>   ## fix the fast time constant `tau` at a known value model_fixed <- nls(     x ~ SSbiexponential(t, A, B, tau = 5, B2, tau2),     data = data,     algorithm = "port",     lower = c(-Inf, -Inf, -Inf, 0),     control = nls.control(warnOnly = TRUE) ) summary(model_fixed) #>  #> Formula: x ~ SSbiexponential(t, A, B, tau = 5, B2, tau2) #>  #> Parameters: #>      Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> A     70.6684     0.4846  145.83   <2e-16 *** #> B     40.1496     0.5232   76.74   <2e-16 *** #> B2    60.2161     0.3239  185.93   <2e-16 *** #> tau2  41.8121     2.4865   16.82   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.7503 on 117 degrees of freedom #>  #> Algorithm "port", convergence message: both X-convergence and relative convergence (5) #>

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
text: Creates initial coefficient estimates selfStart wrapper around exponential_drift(), use stats::nls(). Supports 5-parameter (, B, tau, slope_B, drift_fraction) 6-parameter forms adding time delay TD; arity inferred formula passed stats::nls().

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
code: SSexponential_drift(t, A, B, tau, slope_B, drift_fraction, TD)

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
text: t numeric vector predictor variable (time). numeric parameter starting baseline response variable. B numeric parameter ending asymptote response variable. tau numeric parameter time constant (\(\tau\)) exponential response, units predictor variable t. slope_B numeric parameter linear drift rate dx/dt secondary phase, response units per unit predictor variable t. drift_fraction numeric fraction primary amplitude B - (0.5, 1) linear drift begins, primary response reaches + drift_fraction * (B - ). TD numeric parameter time delay onset exponential response, units predictor variable t. NULL (default), 3-parameter model without time delay used.

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
text: numeric vector predicted values length predictor variable t.

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
text: 5-parameter: x ~ SSexponential_drift(t, , B, tau, slope_B, drift_fraction) 6-parameter: x ~ SSexponential_drift(t, , B, tau, slope_B, drift_fraction, TD) hinge drift onset TD - tau * log(1 - drift_fraction) differentiable, algorithm = "port" tau (TD) bounded non-negative control = nls.control(warnOnly = TRUE) recommended. Starting estimates profiled coarse grid tau (TD) , B, slope_B solved least squares grid point, keeping residual-minimising start. model function returns analytic gradient (one-sided hinge) free parameters "gradient" attribute, stats::nls() resort stats::numericDeriv(). stats::predict() fitted model carries attribute; drop .vector().

title: Self-starting exponential-drift model — SSexponential_drift
text: parameter may held constant writing value place name formula, e.g. x ~ SSexponential_drift(t, , B, tau, slope_B, drift_fraction = 0.95) holds drift onset 95% amplitude (TD + 3 * tau). Fixed parameters excluded estimation returned stats::coef().

title: Biexponential function — biexponential
text: expected response fast excursion toward minimum maximum short B, followed slow recovery back stable plateau B2. excursion point texc occurs two phase rates cancel: texc = TD + log(ratio) / (1 / tau - 1 / tau2) ratio = -(B - ) * tau2 / ((B2 - B) * tau), exists amplitudes oppose sign fast phase dominates onset (ratio > 1). B B2, response monotonic still two-phase.

Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> A     69.5786     0.5490  126.73   <2e-16 *** #> B     39.2594     1.1326   34.66   <2e-16 *** #> tau    5.3301     0.3158   16.88   <2e-16 *** #> B2    59.8830     0.3273  182.97   <2e-16 *** #> tau2  37.8230     3.0486   12.41   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 0.7114 on 116 degrees of freedom #>  #> Algorithm "port", convergence message: relative convergence (4) #>   y <- predict(model, data)  # \donttest{     if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {         ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(t, x)) +             theme_mnirs() +             ggplot2::geom_point() +             ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = y))     }  # }

Default seq_along(x). idx numeric vector indices t calculate local windows. indices t default, can used calculate known indices, invalid values x. width integer defining local window number samples around idx perform operation, according align. span numeric value defining local window time span around idx perform operation, according align. units time_channel t. align Window alignment "centre"/"center" (default), "left", "right". "left" forward looking, "right" backward looking current sample. env calling environment defused call, used report errors warnings coming user-facing function rather validator. v numeric vector sum within windows. Callers centre v first contain floating-point cancellation error. bounds list() start end window index vectors compute_window_bounds(). min_n lower bound returned number samples. x numeric vector response variable. min_obs minimum number samples window must span return value. Shorter (partial) windows return NA. window_idx list shorter length x numeric vectors sample indices local rolling windows. fn function pass local rolling calculation. ... Additional arguments. m numeric matrix one column per rolling window, padded NA windows extend beyond data. outlier_cutoff numeric value local outlier threshold, number standard deviations local median. Default NULL replace outliers. Lower values sensitive flag outliers; higher values conservative. outlier_cutoff = 3 Pearson's 3 sigma edit rule. outlier_cutoff = 2 approximates Tukey-style 1.5*IQR rule. outlier_cutoff = 0 Tukey's median filter. verbose Logical. text: local rolling window can specified either width number samples, span time span units t. Specifying width often faster span. align defaults "centre" local window around idx [idx - floor((width-1)/2), idx + floor(width/2)] width specified. Even width values bias align "left", unequal sample forward idx, effectively returning NA last sample index. span specified, local window [t - span/2, t + span/2]. window_min_obs() converts span sample count via estimated sample rate, less two samples buffer irregular t start end window. compute_local_mean() computes window means O(n) via window_sums(). title: Correct for blood volume changes — correct_blood_volume
text: least two oxy_channel, deoxy_channel, total_channel must specified calculate blood volume correction factor. Best practice specify existing channels data. Missing channels derived specified pair correction applied. total = oxy + deoxy oxy   = total - deoxy deoxy = total - oxy Multiple channel pairs can corrected one call passing equal-length vectors, element number forming pair (e.g. oxy_channel = c(o2hb_1, o2hb_2), deoxy_channel = c(hhb_1, hhb_2)). NOTE: returned data frame include corrected values specified channels. Non-specified channels remain uncorrected therefore longer comparable corrected channels. Best practice specify existing channels data.

title: Correct for blood volume changes — correct_blood_volume
text: NIRS channels negative values, specified channels ensemble-shifted common offset channels contain positive values. Relative scaling across channels preserved. modified method Beever & Tripp et al, 2020 properly calculate total[haem] blood volume correction factor beta negative NIRS values. correction factor beta effectively single-channel fractional (%) oxygen saturation used normalise oxy[haem] deoxy[haem] relative adjusted invariant total[haem]. computed cumulative sum adjusted incremental differences: $$\Delta\text{O2Hb}_c = \Delta\text{O2Hb} - \beta \cdot \Delta\text{THb}$$ $$\Delta\text{HHb}_c = \Delta\text{HHb} - (1 - \beta) \cdot \Delta\text{THb}$$ correction, total[haem] zero (blood volume changes normalised).

title: Exponential-drift function — exponential_drift
text: 5-parameter: + (B - ) * (1 - exp(-t / tau)) + slope_B * pmax(t + tau * log(1 - drift_fraction), 0) 6-parameter: + (B - ) * (1 - exp(-pmax(t - TD, 0) / tau)) + slope_B * pmax(t - TD + tau * log(1 - drift_fraction), 0) , B, tau, TD monoexponential(). drift onset free estimate: secondary drift exactly zero TD - tau * log(1 - drift_fraction) (TD = 0 absent), drift_fraction = 0.95 places onset TD + 3 * tau. excursion point texc drift rate overtakes decaying primary rate, TD + tau * log(|B - | / (|slope_B| * tau)), floored drift onset.

Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> A       10.305631   0.558620   18.45   <2e-16 *** #> B       99.612728   0.302186  329.64   <2e-16 *** #> tau     12.062878   0.202335   59.62   <2e-16 *** #> slope_B -0.495293   0.005346  -92.64   <2e-16 *** #> TD      14.956965   0.167821   89.12   <2e-16 *** #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 2.091 on 175 degrees of freedom #>  #> Algorithm "port", convergence message: relative convergence (4) #>   y <- predict(model, data)  # \donttest{     if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {         ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(t, x)) +             theme_mnirs() +             ggplot2::geom_point() +             ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = y))     }  # }

title: Apply a Butterworth digital filter — filter_butterworth
text: Applies centred (two-pass symmetrical) Butterworth digital filter signal::butter() signal::filtfilt(). Filter type defines desired signal frequencies either passed rejected output signal. Low-pass high-pass filters allow frequencies lower higher cutoff frequency W passed output signal, respectively. Stop-band defines critical range frequencies rejected output signal. Pass-band defines critical range frequencies passed output signal. filter order (number passes) defined order, typically range order = [1, 10]. Higher filter order tends capture rapid changes amplitude, also causes distortion around change points signal. General advice use lowest filter order sufficiently captures desired rapid responses data. critical (cutoff) frequency defined W, numeric value low-pass high-pass filters, two-element vector c(low, high) defining lower upper bands stop-band pass-band filters. W represents desired fractional cutoff frequency range W = [0, 1], 1 Nyquist frequency, .e., half sample rate data Hz. Missing values (NA) x cause error unless na.rm = TRUE. NAs ignored passed returned vector.

B numeric parameter ending asymptote response variable. xmid numeric parameter time inflection point (steepest point) curve, units predictor variable t. slope numeric parameter response rate dx/dt inflection xmid.

title: Gompertz growth functions — gompertz
text: gompertz() (right-Gompertz) asymmetric inflection point xmid closer starting asymptote : early acceleration away , slow approach ending asymptote B. Appropriate fast-onset, slow-tail responses. gompertz_left() (left-Gompertz) inflection point closer ending asymptote B: slow departure , late acceleration toward B. Appropriate slow-onset, fast-tail responses.

title: Gompertz growth functions — gompertz
text: forms re-parameterised xmid time inflection slope response rate dx/dt inflection, k = slope * e / (B - ). gompertz(): + (B - ) * exp(-exp(-k * (t - xmid))). Inflection height fixed + (B - ) / e; 36.8% amplitude. gompertz_left(): + (B - ) * (1 - exp(-exp(k * (t - xmid)))). Inflection height fixed + (B - ) * (1 - 1/e); 63.2% amplitude.

title: Generalised logistic function — logistic
text: 5-parameter Richards form exported advanced use directly stats::nls() used analyse_kinetics() due convergence instability. asymmetric responses, prefer gompertz() / gompertz_left(), stable.

title: Generalised logistic function — logistic
text: forms re-parameterised Richards generalised logistic model xmid time inflection slope response rate dx/dt inflection. 4-parameter (symmetric): + (B - ) / (1 + exp(-4 * slope * (t - xmid) / (B - ))) 5-parameter (asymmetric): + (B - ) / (1 + exp(-k * (t - xmid)))^(1 / v) v = -log(2) / log(asym) k = 2 * slope * v / ((B - ) * asym). inflection t = xmid dx/dt = slope y(xmid) = + (B - ) * asym asym (0, 1): asym = 0.5 (v = 1) collapses 4-parameter form. asym -> 0 gives early-acceleration curve (inflection near ). asym -> 1 gives late-acceleration curve (inflection near B). asym = 0.368 (1/e) approximates right-inflection gompertz() curve. asym = 0.632 (1 - 1/e) approximates left-inflection gompertz_left() curve.

Error t value Pr(>|t|)     #> A      10.2987     0.5316  19.372  < 2e-16 *** #> B     100.9565     0.9135 110.519  < 2e-16 *** #> xmid   29.3426     2.5692  11.421 3.87e-16 *** #> slope   3.8707     0.6245   6.198 7.69e-08 *** #> asym    0.2743     0.1115   2.460    0.017 *   #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1 #>  #> Residual standard error: 1.827 on 55 degrees of freedom #>  #> Number of iterations to convergence: 5  #> Achieved convergence tolerance: 1.54e-06 #>   y <- predict(model, data)  # \donttest{     if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {         ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(t, x)) +             theme_mnirs() +             ggplot2::geom_point() +             ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = y))     }  # }

title: Replace outliers, invalid, and missing values in mnirs data — replace_mnirs

title: Replace outliers, invalid, and missing values in mnirs data — replace_mnirs
text: outlier_cutoff number (MAD-normalised) standard deviations local median. Higher values conservative; lower values flag outliers. outlier_cutoff = 3 – Pearson's 3 sigma edit rule (default). outlier_cutoff = 2 – approximately Tukey-style 1.5*IQR rule. outlier_cutoff = 0 – Tukey's median filter (every point replaced local median).

title: Replace outliers, invalid, and missing values in mnirs data — replace_mnirs
text: method = "linear" method = "locf" use stats::approx() rule = 2, leading NAs filled "nocb" ("next observation carried backward") trailing NAs "locf". method = "median" calculates local median valid (non-NA) values either side NAs, within window defined width (number samples) span (time span units t). Sequential NAs replaced median value.

code: ## vectorised operations x <- c(1, 999, 3, 4, 999, 6) replace_invalid(x, invalid_values = 999, width = 3, method = "median") #> [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6  (x_na <- replace_outliers(x, outlier_cutoff = 3, width = 3, method = "none")) #> [1]  1 NA  3  4 NA  6  replace_missing(x_na, method = "linear") #> [1] 1 2 3 4 5 6  ## read example data data <- read_mnirs(     file_path = example_mnirs("moxy_ramp"),     nirs_channels = c(smo2 = "SmO2 Live"),     time_channel = c(time = "hh:mm:ss"),     verbose = FALSE )  ## clean data data_clean <- replace_mnirs(     data,                  ## channels retrieved from metadata     invalid_values = 0,    ## known invalid values in the data     invalid_above = 90,    ## remove data spikes above 90     outlier_cutoff = 3,    ## Pearson's 3 sigma edit rule     width = 7,            ## window for outlier detection and interpolation     method = "linear"      ## linear interpolation over NAs )  # \donttest{   if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {     ## plot original and show where values have been replaced     ## ignore warning about replacing the existing colour scale     plot(data, time_labels = TRUE) +       ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(         name = NULL,         breaks = c("smo2", "replaced"),         values = palette_mnirs(2)       ) +       ggplot2::geom_point(         data = data[data_clean$smo2 != data$smo2, ],         ggplot2::aes(y = smo2, colour = "replaced"),         na.rm = TRUE       ) +       ggplot2::geom_line(         data = {           data_clean[!is.na(data$smo2), "smo2"] <- NA           data_clean         },         ggplot2::aes(y = smo2, colour = "replaced"),         linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE       )   } #> Scale for colour is already present. #> Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.  # }

title: mnirs 0.8.0
text: initial release analyse_kinetics() family kinetics modelling functions!

title: mnirs 0.8.0
text: analyse_kinetics() fits oxygenation response kinetics parametric non-parametric methods. accepts single “mnirs” data frame, list data frames, grouped data frame, analyses nirs_channels interval, returns formatted table results. See ?analyse_kinetics canonical (.e. human-verified) documentation methods, arguments, returned objects. method argument selects kinetics model. additional arguments: "response_time" — non-parametric fractional (e.g. 50%) response time. "peak_slope" — peak rolling linear least-squares regression slope. "monoexponential" — 3- 4-parameter exponential curve fit via stats::nls(). "exponential_drift" — two-phase fast monoexponential primary response plus slow linear secondary drift. "biexponential" — two-phase fast primary slow secondary exponential phases. "sigmoidal" — 4-parameter symmetric generalised logistic Gompertz-family curve. "sigmoidal_drift" — two-phase fast sigmoidal primary response plus slow linear secondary drift. arguments can supplied globally per-channel per-interval. However, method currently accepts single global model channels. Results returned structured list class “mnirs_kinetics”, containing: method: selected kinetics model. model: lm nls objects. coefficients: resultant model parameters. data: input data augmented *_fitted columns per nirs_channel. interval_times: start_times end_times analysed intervals. diagnostics: fit quality model validation parameters used evaluate compare model fits. channel_args: selected per-channel per-interval args. warnings: warning error messages generated fitting. call: matched call. print.mnirs_kinetics() returns formatted coefficients table, plot.mnirs_kinetics() displays observed data overlaid fitted curves channel interval.
code: analyse_kinetics(     data,     nirs_channels = c(smo2_left, smo2_right),     method = "monoexponential",     use_TD = TRUE,      ## use time delay parameter     direction = "auto"  ## auto-detect response direction ) |>      print() |>  ## the formatted table prints the coefficients     plot()      ## plot observations & fitted data

title: mnirs 0.8.0
text: individual fitting methods called analyse_kinetics() can called directly outside “mnirs” data structure: response_time() peak_slope() estimate kinetics directly numeric vector x t, return named list coefficients (lm model object peak_slope()). monoexponential(), exponential_drift(), biexponential(), logistic(), gompertz(), gompertz_left(), sigmoidal_drift() contain parametric equations model response curves. can used construct pure curve explicit parameters, simulate data, plotting fitted model. SSmonoexponential(), SSexponential_drift(), SSbiexponential(), SSlogistic(), SSgompertz(), SSgompertz_left(), SSsigmoidal_drift() matching self-starting (selfStart) wrappers, generate initial parameter estimates can fit directly stats::nls().
code: peak_slope(x, t, width = 5, direction = "auto")  response_time(x, t, response_fraction = c(0.5, 0.632)) t <- 1:100 monoexponential(t, A = 10, B = 100, tau = 8, TD = 15)  sigmoidsl(t, A = 10, B = 100, xmid = 30, slope = 4) nls(x ~ SSmonoexponential(t, A, B, tau, TD), data = data)  nls(x ~ SSlogistic(t, A, B, xmid, slope), data = data)

title: mnirs 0.6.3
text: extract_intervals(): specifying start end by_lap(), start refer first sample lap, end last sample. previous behaviour, start = by_lap() include entire specified lap(s). resulted less control displaying parts lap. Updated behaviour now consistent by_time, by_label, by_sample() methods, reference start end single sample. allows extraction e.g. first 60-sec lap:
code: read_mnirs() |>      extract_intervals(         start = by_lap(1, 3),         span = c(0, 60),     ) ## returns a list of two intervals with the first 60-sec of laps 1 and 3, respectively.

text: filter_mnirs(): Method-specific arguments (e.g. order method = "butterworth", width method = "moving_average") removed generic function call. Continue passed appropriate method via .... Documentation info/warning/abort messages updated. filter_ma() better separates effects partial na.rm args: partial = FALSE default returns NA edges insufficient number samples available compared specified width span. partial = TRUE calculates mean values edges, long one valid non-NA sample available. na.rm = FALSE default behaves expected mean(na.rm = FALSE), propagating NAs local window calculated mean warning.
